newsitem.title: DENMARK: Codan sees 1997 profits same as last year.
newsitem.headline: Codan sees 1997 profits same as last year.

text.p: Denmark's second-biggest insurer A/S Forsikringsselskabet Codan posted improved first half 1997 results on Thursday, boosted by securities earnings and a solid Danish accident performance and forecast that full year profits would be similar to 1996.
"Our expectations for insurance operations the rest of the year are unchanged," Codan said in a statement accompanying its interim results.
"The management forecasts an overall 1997 result before security fluctuations of the same order as last year," it said.

In March, Codan, 71.45 percent owned by Britain's Royal & Sun Alliance reported record full year 1996 net profits of 1.07 billion crowns ($148.8 million), almost double the previous year's 561 million crowns.

Codan posted pre-tax result profits for the first six months of 511 million crowns compared to the same 1996 period's 441 million crowns with net earnings at 6.993 billion crowns against 1996's interim 6.032 billion crowns.

Codan's Danish accident insurance profits for the interim period rose solidly to 415 million crowns from first-half 1996's 289 million crowns, while Swedish and Norwegian operations performed much less impressively.
"We see Danish accident making an operating profit for 1997 similar to last year, with Swedish accident doing better despite a disappointing first-half year," Codan said.
The statement showed falls in profits from life and pension insurance, but increased earnings from foreign exchange and securities compensated for these losses in part, it said.

The market, which had expected higher interim profits, was generally unimpressed by Codan's result and the share fell 30 crowns or around three percent to 1,000 crowns by late morning. -- Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652 ($ = 7.188 Danish Crowns)
